items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Billie was dying then. Just skin and bones.

ctx.x: You recorded in a thing that’s recently been reissued on video and CD . . . that’s being widely discussed again, in The Sound of Jazz, which had Billie Holiday, Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, and many many other legendary jazz figures.

Yeah, all of them dying, most of them. Drank their self or doped their self to death. Billie was dying then. Just skin and bones. Lester Young had been . . . drank so much brandy, ’til his eyes . . . You can see that their eyes look like two . . . something in a bowl . . . look like two eggs in a bowl of milk. Eyes that lost their pupils, he was so drunk. Had to lead him. In that solo you see Lester take with Billie, they had to lead him . . . pick him up, almost, and lead him to the bandstand. When they brought…

Then you recorded with quite a few other people, most recently, in recent years, Wynton Marsalis. What was it like recording with such a wide range of people, going from some of the early jazz pioneers to some of the latest up and coming . . .

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I never got to know Billie personally

ctx.x: So I was at the Mad House. I told you about that Chicken Cock whiskey... So there I saw Billie for the first time. I never got to know Billie personally, because I had been involved with young ladies who knew Billie and I'd hear about Billie, and...um, from then on, she went on. But Billie always knew the right people. In fact, she knew too many right people. She knew the right people, the wrong people, and she always had a group of people with her, because she was a fascinating young lady.

You'd see Billie with maybe three Mexicans one night. Tomorrow you'd see her with some Chinese. Some cat from Georgia somewhere. You'd see her with some... Always with some people with them dark glasses. Later on you wouldn't see her with a man. You'd always see her with a dog. The last dog she had, his name was Mister. Yeah, Mister. She used to go to Creole Pete's Restaurant with Mister, and sit with Mister at a table, and if you were half-drunk and you looked over there, you would think it was some little…
